headline: Highest risk is medium: ComfyUI can ingest files while awesome-python is a non-runnable docs-only collection, so interaction risks are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a docs-only, non-runnable collection, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. B can read files and uses an asynchronous queue, but no shared channel or default bridge is documented. Any prompt-injection pathway would require unusual manual copy-paste or external orchestration, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated text into a downstream prompt or file consumed by another agent, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added outside these profiles, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep B outputs in a separate folder from any prompt inputs.
Add a human review step before reusing generated text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, while B is offline by default with vendor-only egress and no secrets handled. B can read model files, but there is no documented shared workspace or sensitive data flow from A. Leakage risk is therefore limited and not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in B's model directories, B may process them as local inputs.
IF an external orchestrator shares a workspace between A and B, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not store sensitive files in B's model folders.
Use separate OS users for each agent.
Disable any external file sync into the shared environment.
Review B outputs before exporting them outside the host.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no write or network surfaces; B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping mutable write capability, there is no plausible capability-conflict pathway in the documented pair.
conditions: IF an external wrapper grants either agent shared write access, conflict risk would need re-evaluation.
mitigations: Keep both agents on read-only mounts where possible.
Do not grant shared git credentials.
Run B in a separate container from any mutable workspace.
requires-engineering: add lockfiles if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A does not produce executable actions and B is an image-generation system that can operate offline. There is no documented default chain where B treats A as authoritative input, so cascading error is mainly a manual workflow issue rather than an inherent pairwise hazard.
conditions: IF an operator feeds A’s curated text directly into B prompts without verification, downstream errors can propagate.
IF B outputs are auto-posted or auto-acted on by another system, the cascade becomes more serious.
mitigations: Verify any text copied from A before using it in B.
Keep a checklist for prompt provenance.
Require human approval before publishing B outputs.
requires-engineering: add validation for any automated handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention obligations are documented for either agent. A is a docs-only collection and B is offline-capable with no secrets handled, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either workflow, compliance must be reassessed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both workflows.
Document any future data residency requirements.
Review retention settings before enabling shared storage.
